summary: Black Angel is a heavy euro where players use dice as workers to explore a shrinking, tile-based spaceship map, gathering resources and completing contracts while racing to reach planet Spes before the Ravager deck runs out. Despite the cooperative-sounding theme, it's a competitive point-salad race with tight turn efficiency puzzles and a constant push against the game's own countdown clock.
praised: innovative dice-as-workers mechanic with meaningful dice manipulation
tense shared countdown (map reduction / Ravager deck) that pressures every turn
strong production values and thematic artwork/sculpts
criticised: dense, icon-heavy rulebook with a steep learning curve
some luck from dice rolls even with mitigation options
can feel more solitaire/parallel than interactive for a 'shared ship' theme

interaction.kind: indirect competition for shared tiles/worker spots and racing the shrinking map

scoring.why: points come from exploring/claiming tiles, completing contracts, combat tokens, and end-game bonuses, so efficient multi-source engine building decides the winner
